title: 96% of counties counted moved left since 2024
dek: Every county with a Senate or governor race on Tuesday, drawn as a block whose height is how far it moved from the Harris–Trump vote. 2,673 of 2,775 moved toward the Democrats, the typical one by 14 points; all 254 Texas counties did, Starr County by 72. Plus the night as it happened, seat by seat.

areas.title: The border counties that swung hardest
areas.dek: Starr County moved 72 points. The Rio Grande Valley and the counties along the border, which went for Trump two years ago, came back to the Democrats harder than anywhere else in the country.

areas.title: The Southeast: every county in four states, and most of Florida
areas.dek: Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina and Virginia moved left in every county. Florida moved too, even as it stayed red.

areas.title: The Midwest: Ohio, Iowa and Kansas flip
areas.dek: Three Senate seats Trump carried by double digits changed hands. The swing ran from the Great Lakes to the Kansas prairie, meatpacking towns included.

areas.title: The Deep South and Appalachia: the reddest counties moved too
areas.dek: Republicans held every seat here but Mississippi’s, and every county still moved toward the Democrats, most of them by 15 to 25 points.

areas.title: Where the map moved right
areas.dek: Only 101 counties moved toward the Republicans. They are in Vermont, Maine, upstate New York and a few corners of Maryland, and most of them have a governor to thank.

border.title: The wall, and the counties around it
border.dek: Every one of the 24 counties on the Mexican border moved toward the Democrats, Starr County by 72 points and the border as a whole by a median 30. In the state that redrew its map to send five more Republicans to Washington, the border is where the plan came apart.

states.name: Texas
states.title: Every Texas county moved left as Talarico broke the GOP's statewide streak
states.dek: James Talarico beat Ken Paxton by 12.1 points, a 25.8-point move from Donald Trump's 2024 margin. The swing ran from Paxton's own suburbs to the Panhandle. It was smallest in the reddest, least populous counties.
states.summary: Talarico won by 12.1 points; all 254 counties moved toward Democrats, led by South Texas and the big suburban counties.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.title: All 67 Pennsylvania counties moved toward Shapiro, and 11 Trump counties flipped
states.dek: Gov. Josh Shapiro won a second term by 22 points, a 24-point move from Donald Trump's 2024 margin. The biggest moves came in the southwestern gas counties and the northeastern coal valleys. The smallest came in the most Republican rural counties.
states.summary: Shapiro won by 22 points; every county moved left, typically by 23 points, and 11 counties Trump carried flipped.

states.name: Rhode Island
states.title: Every Rhode Island county swings left; Reed wins sixth term by 37
states.dek: Sen. Jack Reed beat a little-known Republican by 37.5 points, 23.6 points better than Kamala Harris did in 2024. The biggest moves came in Providence County and in Kent County, which was the state's closest county two years ago.
states.summary: Reed's 37.5-point win moved all five counties left, led by Providence (+26) and Kent (+24), with turnout at 70% of 2024's.

states.name: Mississippi
states.title: Every Mississippi county moved left as Colom edges ahead of Hyde-Smith
states.dek: Scott Colom leads Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 2,574 votes, and the race has not been called. The biggest moves came in the Memphis suburbs, Hattiesburg and the Gulf Coast. The smallest came in Delta counties that were already heavily Democratic.
states.summary: A 23-point move left puts Colom 2,574 votes ahead of Hyde-Smith in an uncalled race; all 82 counties shifted toward Democrats.

states.name: North Carolina
states.title: Every North Carolina county moved left as Roy Cooper won by nearly 20
states.dek: The former governor turned a state Donald Trump carried by 3 points into a 19.6-point Senate win. The shift was almost the same size in mountain hollows, exurbs and cities, and largest where turnout fell furthest.
states.summary: Roy Cooper won by 19.6 points; all 100 counties moved left, 21 flipped from Trump, and the shift was nearly uniform.

states.name: South Carolina
states.title: South Carolina's Republican Upstate moved furthest as Andrews took the Graham seat
states.dek: Every one of South Carolina's 46 counties moved toward the Democrats. Spartanburg and the Upstate's Republican strongholds moved the most. Hilton Head and the southern coast moved the least, and Republicans held the governor's office on the same ballot.
states.summary: All 46 counties moved left; Annie Andrews won by 4.5 points as Greenville, York and 11 other Trump counties flipped.

states.name: Hawaii
states.title: Josh Green's record win pushes every Hawaii county 20-plus points left
states.dek: Gov. Josh Green won a second term by 45 points, 22 points better than Kamala Harris did in Hawaii in 2024. Kauai moved the most. A quarter fewer ballots were cast, so lower turnout is part of the story.
states.summary: Green's 45-point reelection margin moved Hawaii 22 points left of 2024; Kauai led every county with a 29-point swing.

states.name: West Virginia
states.title: Capito wins a third term as all 55 West Virginia counties move left
states.dek: Sen. Shelley Moore Capito won by about 20 points, half of Donald Trump's 2024 margin. Her Democratic challenger carried Charleston, Morgantown and Jefferson County, and the biggest shift came in Berkeley County in the Eastern Panhandle.
states.summary: Capito won by 20.4 points, down from Trump's 41.9; all 55 counties moved left, and three flipped Democratic.

states.name: New Jersey
states.title: Booker's 27-point win moved all 21 New Jersey counties left
states.dek: Cory Booker turned Kamala Harris's 5.9-point 2024 margin into a 27-point win and carried seven counties Donald Trump had won. The biggest moves came where turnout fell furthest: Hudson, Passaic and Ocean.
states.summary: Booker won by 27.3 points, a 21-point move from 2024; all 21 counties moved left and seven Trump counties flipped.

states.name: Alabama
states.title: Every Alabama county moved left, and Barry Moore still won by nine
states.dek: Republican Barry Moore beat Everett Wess by 9.4 points, compared with Trump's 30.6 in 2024. Madison, Mobile and Tuscaloosa counties flipped. The Black Belt moved least, and turnout fell furthest in the northern hill country.
states.summary: All 67 counties moved toward Democrats; Barry Moore won the Senate seat by 9.4 points as six Trump counties flipped.

states.name: Kansas
states.title: Every Kansas county moved left; the southwest moved furthest
states.dek: Adam Hamilton beat Sen. Roger Marshall by 5.1 points in a state Donald Trump carried by 16.1, a 21-point move. Meatpacking counties hit by September immigration raids moved most; the governor's race is still uncalled.
states.summary: Hamilton won by 5.1 points; all 105 counties moved left, Seward by 52 points, and six Trump counties flipped.

states.name: New Mexico
states.title: Every New Mexico county moved left as Luján won by 26 points
states.dek: Sen. Ben Ray Luján beat a Republican who got on the ballot through write-in votes. Every county moved toward the Democrats and five Trump counties flipped, a bigger shift than in Deb Haaland's governor's race.
states.summary: Luján won by 26.5 points; all 33 counties moved left and five that Trump won in 2024 flipped.

states.name: Georgia
states.title: All 159 Georgia counties moved toward Ossoff, from Dalton to DeKalb
states.dek: Two years after Donald Trump carried Georgia, Jon Ossoff won a second Senate term by 18 points. The move reached every county, was largest in the north Georgia counties with many Hispanic residents and in the Atlanta suburbs, and was smallest in the southwest.
states.summary: Ossoff won Georgia by 18 points, a 20-point move from 2024, and all 159 counties moved toward the Democrats.

states.name: Louisiana
states.title: Every Louisiana parish moved left, but Julia Letlow held the Senate seat
states.dek: Democrat Jamie Davis, a Tensas Parish farmer, cut Donald Trump's 22-point margin to 1.8 and flipped eight parishes. Some of the biggest swings came in the Republican suburbs of New Orleans and Baton Rouge.
states.summary: Julia Letlow won by 1.8 points as all 64 parishes moved left, a 20-point swing from Trump's 2024 margin.

states.name: Arkansas
states.title: Cotton holds Arkansas as all 75 counties move toward the Democrats
states.dek: Tom Cotton won a third term by 11.9 points, compared with Donald Trump's 30.6 in 2024. The biggest shifts came in Northwest Arkansas, Jonesboro and De Queen. The smallest came in the Delta counties that already vote Democratic.
states.summary: Cotton won by 11.9 points, down from Trump's 30.6; all 75 counties moved left and Washington and Desha flipped.

states.name: Arizona
states.title: Every Arizona county swings toward Hobbs as Maricopa and Yuma flip
states.dek: Gov. Katie Hobbs beat Andy Biggs by 13 points, an 18.7-point swing from Donald Trump's 2024 win. All 15 counties moved toward the Democrats. Maricopa flipped, and so did Yuma, where the count is still partial.
states.summary: Hobbs wins by 13.1 points; all 15 counties move left, and Maricopa and Yuma flip from Trump.

states.name: Kentucky
states.title: Eastern Kentucky moved most as Barr held McConnell's seat by 12
states.dek: All 120 Kentucky counties moved toward Democrat Charles Booker compared with Donald Trump's 2024 margins, and Franklin County flipped. Republican Andy Barr still won by 12 points. The mountain counties moved the most, and Lake Cumberland and the far west moved the least.
states.summary: Barr won by 12.1 points, 18.5 closer than Trump's 2024 margin; all 120 counties moved left, and Franklin County flipped.

states.name: Tennessee
states.title: Hagerty holds Tennessee as Murfreesboro, Clarksville and Chattanooga swing away
states.dek: Bill Hagerty won a second Senate term by 12 points, but all 95 counties moved toward the Democrats from 2024, and three metro counties (Rutherford, Montgomery and Hamilton) narrowly went for Marquita Bradshaw.
states.summary: Hagerty won by 12.2 points, but all 95 counties moved left; Rutherford, Montgomery and Hamilton flipped to Bradshaw.

states.name: Iowa
states.title: Iowa's 99 counties all moved left as Turek took the Senate seat
states.dek: Josh Turek won by 4.1 points in a state Donald Trump carried by 13.3 two years ago. Every county shifted toward the Democrats, most in Crawford and Wapello counties and least in the state's far northwest corner.
states.summary: Turek flips Iowa's Senate seat by 4.1 points; all 99 counties moved left, ten flipped, and Pottawattamie went narrowly Democratic.

states.name: Virginia
states.title: All 133 Virginia localities moved toward Warner, from Manassas to the coalfields
states.dek: Mark Warner won a fourth Senate term by about 23 points, 17 more than Kamala Harris's 2024 margin. The biggest swings came in Prince William County and its two cities, and in Southwest Virginia, where turnout fell most.
states.summary: Warner won by 22.7 points; all 133 counties and cities moved left, 11 flipped from Trump, none the other way.

states.name: Oklahoma
states.title: Every Oklahoma county moved left, but Kevin Hern still won by 18
states.dek: All 77 counties shifted toward the Democrats from 2024. Oklahoma and Cleveland counties flipped. The biggest swings came in the Panhandle, the Oklahoma City suburbs and a band of southern and eastern counties.
states.summary: Hern won by 17.9 points, about half Trump's margin; all 77 counties moved left, and Oklahoma and Cleveland counties flipped.

states.name: Ohio
states.title: Brown retakes Ohio as all 88 counties move toward Democrats
states.dek: Sherrod Brown beat Jon Husted by 4.9 points in a state Donald Trump carried by 11. The biggest moves came in small, deep-red Appalachian counties where turnout fell the most. Eight Trump counties flipped.
states.summary: Brown wins by 4.9 points, a 16-point move from 2024; all 88 counties shift left, eight flip, Appalachian counties move most.

states.name: Wyoming
states.title: All 23 Wyoming counties moved toward Byrd; Hageman still won by 30
states.dek: Harriet Hageman won Wyoming's open Senate seat by 30.5 points, about 16 points less than Donald Trump's 2024 margin. Albany County, home to Laramie, flipped. Sweetwater, Natrona and Laramie counties moved the most.
states.summary: Hageman won Wyoming's Senate seat by 30.5 points, down from Trump's 46; all 23 counties moved left and Albany flipped.

states.name: Colorado
states.title: Every Colorado county moved left; El Paso and Douglas went Democratic
states.dek: John Hickenlooper won a second Senate term by 25 points, more than twice Kamala Harris's 2024 margin. The biggest moves came in Adams County, Weld County and the San Luis Valley. The smallest came in tiny, deeply Republican counties.
states.summary: Hickenlooper won by 25 points; all 64 counties moved left, and eight Trump counties, including El Paso and Douglas, flipped.

states.name: Nebraska
states.title: Every Nebraska county moved toward Osborn, but Ricketts held on
states.dek: All 93 counties voted to the left of their 2024 presidential result, Sarpy flipped, and the biggest moves came in packing-plant and Panhandle counties. But Dan Osborn's statewide deficit looks a lot like his 2024 loss.
states.summary: All 93 Nebraska counties moved toward independent Dan Osborn and Sarpy flipped, but Pete Ricketts won by 6.2 points.

states.name: Alaska
states.title: Alaska swings with the nation, leaving Peltola and Sullivan nearly tied
states.dek: Mary Peltola leads Sen. Dan Sullivan by 637 votes with about three-quarters of the expected vote counted, a 14-point move from 2024. Roughly 75,000 uncounted ballots and a likely ranked-choice tabulation are still ahead.
states.summary: Peltola leads Sullivan by 637 votes, a 14-point move left from 2024; uncounted ballots and ranked choices remain.

states.name: Idaho
states.title: Ada County flips as Idaho's Senate margin shrinks by 13 points
states.dek: Republican Jim Risch won a fourth term by 23 points over independent Todd Achilles. Still, 43 of Idaho's 44 counties moved left of their 2024 presidential vote, with the biggest moves in the east and the south-central counties.
states.summary: Risch won by 23 points, 13.5 points closer than Trump's 2024 margin; Ada County flipped, and only Latah moved right.

states.name: Illinois
states.title: Chicago's suburbs swing hardest as Stratton wins Illinois by 24 points
states.dek: Juliana Stratton's Senate margin more than doubled Kamala Harris's 2024 showing. Cook County and the collar counties moved 14 to 18 points; much of rural downstate barely budged, and a few western counties moved toward Republicans.
states.summary: Stratton won by 24 points, 13 better than Harris, with Chicago and its suburbs moving most; McHenry and Sangamon flipped.

states.name: Delaware
states.title: Coons carries Sussex as Delaware moves 12 points toward Democrats
states.dek: Chris Coons won a fourth Senate term by 27 points. All three of Delaware's counties moved toward Democrats by similar amounts, and Republican Sussex County voted for him for the first time.
states.summary: Coons won by 27.1 points, a 12.4-point move from 2024, and Sussex County flipped from Trump to the Democrat.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.title: New Hampshire moved left everywhere, but kept its Republican governor
states.dek: All ten counties moved toward Democrat Chris Pappas, who won the open Senate seat by nearly 14 points and flipped Rockingham, Carroll and Sullivan counties. On the same ballots, Gov. Kelly Ayotte won a second term by about four.
states.summary: Every county moved left as Chris Pappas won the Senate seat by 13.7 points, while Republican Kelly Ayotte held the governorship.

states.name: Nevada
states.title: Clark County's 13-point swing puts Aaron Ford in Nevada's governor's office
states.dek: Democrat Aaron Ford unseated Gov. Joe Lombardo in a state Donald Trump carried two years ago. Fifteen of Nevada's 17 counties moved left, but most of the swing came from Las Vegas, and no county changed sides.
states.summary: Aaron Ford beats Gov. Joe Lombardo by 7.7 points as Clark County moves 13 points left and Douglas County moves right.

states.name: California
states.title: California moves 10 points left as inland counties swing back to Democrats
states.dek: Xavier Becerra won the governor's race by about 30 points with 71 percent of the expected vote counted. Nine counties Donald Trump carried in 2024, from Riverside to Imperial, now show Democratic leads.
states.summary: Becerra won by 30 points in the count so far, 10 better than Harris; nine Trump counties flipped.

states.name: Florida
states.title: Miami-Dade and Osceola led Florida's swing; The Villages went the other way
states.dek: Ashley Moody held Florida's Senate seat by 2.9 points in a state Donald Trump carried by 13.1. Sixty-six of 67 counties moved toward Angie Nixon, and seven Trump counties flipped, from Jacksonville to Kissimmee.
states.summary: Moody won by 2.9 points after a 10-point swing; Miami-Dade, Osceola and five other Trump counties flipped, while Sumter moved right.

states.name: Montana
states.title: Helena and Livingston flip as Montana shifts left, but Alme wins
states.dek: Independent Seth Bodnar ran 9 points better than Kamala Harris did in 2024 and carried two counties Trump had won. Republican Kurt Alme still won by about 11 points while Bodnar and the Democratic nominee split the opposition.
states.summary: Montana moved 9 points left in its Senate race, but Republican Kurt Alme won by 10.6 against a divided opposition.

states.name: Wisconsin
states.title: Crowley wins Wisconsin by 8 as Brown, Kenosha and Racine flip
states.dek: David Crowley's win for governor moved 71 of Wisconsin's 72 counties toward Democrats compared with 2024. Milwaukee and the mid-sized cities led the shift, while Tom Tiffany's Northwoods home barely moved.
states.summary: Crowley won by 8 points, an 8.9-point move from Trump's 2024 edge; seven counties flipped and none went Republican.

states.name: Michigan
states.title: In Michigan, all 83 counties moved left; Wayne and Macomb led
states.dek: Abdul El-Sayed won the open Senate seat by 7.1 points in a state Donald Trump carried by 1.4. The largest moves came in metro Detroit, where Wayne and Macomb counties swung 12 to 14 points.
states.summary: Michigan: El-Sayed wins by 7.1 as all 83 counties move left, led by Wayne and Macomb in metro Detroit.

states.name: South Dakota
states.title: Black Hills tilt toward independent Bengs as Rounds holds South Dakota
states.dek: Sen. Mike Rounds won a third term by 21 points, eight fewer than Donald Trump's 2024 margin. The shift was sharpest around Rapid City and Sioux Falls, while reservation counties and the Pierre area moved the other way.
states.summary: Rounds beat independent Brian Bengs by 21 points, an 8-point shift from 2024, led by the Black Hills and Sioux Falls.

states.name: New York
states.title: The city swung back to Hochul; the north country kept drifting right
states.dek: Kathy Hochul won by 19.6 points, seven better than Kamala Harris, on big leftward moves in the Bronx, Queens and the suburbs. Half of New York's counties moved the other way, nearly a third of all right-moving counties nationwide.
states.summary: Hochul won by 19.6 points on surging city and suburban margins, while 31 counties, mostly upstate, moved toward Republicans.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.title: Every Massachusetts county moved toward Markey, Bristol most of all
states.dek: Edward Markey won a third full term by a wider margin than Kamala Harris had in 2024. The biggest moves came in the closest counties, especially on the South Coast, and in places where fewer 2024 voters returned.
states.summary: Markey widened the Democratic margin in all 14 counties, by 11 points in Bristol and by just one on Cape Cod.

states.name: Minnesota
states.title: In Minnesota, the regional cities moved most as Flanagan won by 10
states.dek: Peggy Flanagan beat Michele Tafoya by 10.1 points, about six points better than Kamala Harris did. The biggest swings came in counties around Duluth, Rochester, Moorhead, Austin and Worthington. The deep-red countryside moved far less, and one suburb moved the other way.
states.summary: Flanagan won by 10.1; regional-city counties like Clay, Mower and Nobles swung hardest, while Carver County moved toward Republicans.

states.name: Oregon
states.title: Every Oregon county moved toward Merkley, while Kotek ran 10 points behind him
states.dek: Jeff Merkley beat Kamala Harris's 2024 margin by five points and carried Marion, Tillamook and Wasco, three counties Donald Trump won. On the same ballots, Gov. Tina Kotek won by less than Harris did.
states.summary: All 36 counties shifted left for Merkley, a modest five-point move, while Kotek trailed Harris's margin in a closer governor's race.

states.name: Connecticut
states.title: Connecticut moves 4.6 points left as Lamont wins a third term
states.dek: Ned Lamont beat Ryan Fazio by 19.1 points, 4.6 points wider than Kamala Harris's 2024 margin. That is a real move, but well short of the 14-point move typical of counties nationally.
states.summary: Ned Lamont won a third term by 19.1 points, a 4.6-point move left of 2024, well below the national typical move.

states.name: Maryland
states.title: Moore widens Maryland margin in D.C. suburbs as Eastern Shore drifts right
states.dek: Gov. Wes Moore ran 2.7 points ahead of Kamala Harris's 2024 margin. That is a small move by this year's national standard. His big gains around Washington and in Western Maryland were partly offset by losses on the Eastern Shore.
states.summary: Moore beat Harris's margin by 2.7 points. The D.C. suburbs and Western Maryland moved left, and the Eastern Shore moved right.

states.name: Maine
states.title: Jackson beat Collins, yet Maine's Senate map came out redder than 2024
states.dek: Troy Jackson unseated Susan Collins by 6.3 points. Even so, 14 of Maine's 16 counties voted more Republican for Senate than they did for president in 2024. That shows how far Collins ran ahead of her party, not that Republicans gained ground.
states.summary: Jackson won by 6.3 points, but Collins ran ahead of Trump, and 14 of 16 counties moved slightly right.

states.name: Vermont
states.title: Vermont's counties all swung right, and the reason was Phil Scott
states.dek: All 14 counties moved toward the Republican column between Kamala Harris's 2024 win and Gov. Phil Scott's sixth-term victory. On the same ballot, voters restored Democratic supermajorities in the Legislature, so the shift tracks one governor more than a party.
states.summary: All 14 counties moved right as Phil Scott won a sixth term by 6.6 points while Democrats gained at the Statehouse.

money.title: The $67 million behind six Senate races, and what it bought
money.dek: A crypto super PAC was the biggest outside spender in The Watch's federal data, and most of its money went into an Alabama primary. The filings so far show only part of what the national players spent.
